qa_pairs.question: What are the four sequential stages of traditional Ethiopian Orthodox church education, and what does the graduation text of the primary stage signify?
qa_pairs.answer: The four sequential stages are: 1) Nebab Bet (School of Reading), 2) Zema Bet (School of Liturgical Music & Sacred Dance), 3) Qene Bet (School of Poetry & Philosophy), and 4) Metsahaf Bet (School of Canonical Books & Law). The graduation text of the Nebab Bet is the 'Dawit' (150 Psalms of David); completing it signified functional literacy and qualified the student as a 'Yeqolo Temari' (scholar-traveler).

qa_pairs.question: Who created the indigenous Ethiopian musical notation system in the 6th century, and what are its three fundamental modal tones?
qa_pairs.answer: Saint Yared of Axum created the indigenous musical notation system in the 6th century CE during the reign of Emperor Gebre Mesqel. The three modal tones are: 1) Ge'ez (plain, steady chant representing the Father), 2) Ezel (solemn, sorrowful chant representing the Son), and 3) Araray (joyful, high-pitched melismatic chant representing the Holy Spirit).

qa_pairs.question: What is the primary natural prey of the Ethiopian Wolf (Canis simensis) on the Sanetti Plateau, and why is this canid specialized compared to other wolves?
qa_pairs.answer: The primary natural prey is the Giant Mole-rat (Tachyoryctes macrocephalus) alongside African Grass Rats (Arvicanthis). Unlike grey wolves that hunt large ungulates in packs, Canis simensis is an extreme morphological specialist with an elongated snout and slender limbs tailored for daytime solitary stalking and excavation of subterranean rodents in the Afro-alpine moorlands.

qa_pairs.question: Why is southwestern Ethiopia considered the global primary center of origin for Coffea arabica, and what genetic reservoir does it shelter?
qa_pairs.answer: Southwestern Ethiopia (regions of Kaffa, Sheka, Yayu, and Bench Maji) is the evolutionary birthplace of Coffea arabica, an allotetraploid (2n = 44) species. Its Afromontane cloud forests shelter over 99% of global wild Arabica genetic diversity, harboring unique wild germplasm critical for breeding resistance to Coffee Berry Disease, Leaf Rust, and low caffeine traits.

qa_pairs.question: When was the first modern secular school opened in Ethiopia, and what languages and subjects were taught?
qa_pairs.answer: Emperor Menelik II opened the Menelik II School in October 1908 at Arat Kilo in Addis Ababa. It recruited Egyptian Coptic educators and taught French (primary diplomatic medium), English, Italian, Arabic, Amharic, mathematics, geography, and sciences.

qa_pairs.question: What indigenous Ethiopian plant was discovered by Professor Aklilu Lemma to fight schistosomiasis (bilharzia), and how does it work?
qa_pairs.answer: Endod (Phytolacca dodecandra / African Soapberry). In 1964, Prof. Aklilu Lemma and Dr. Legesse Wolde-Yohannes discovered that crushed Endod berries release natural triterpenoid saponins (lemmatoxin) that kill freshwater snails carrying the bilharzia parasite at parts-per-million concentrations while naturally biodegrading within 48 hours.
